newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares ease, down trend seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares ease, down trend seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares opened slightly lower on Friday, and traders said the market would continue slightly down for the rest of the day.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index opened slightly off at 298.07 after closing at 298.24 on Thursday.
"Operators decided levels were right for profit-taking after the short-term rise of the market," said acting head trader Evgeny Skibitsky at Rossiisky Kredit Bank.
Skibitsky said the market was in an unstable balance as investors were still cautious about the consequences of possible demonopolisation of natural monopolies UES and Gazprom.
National power utility UES EESR.RTS declined to $0.2072 at GMT 0810 GMT from $0.2080 at closing on Thursday and Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS was off at $5.000 after closing at $5.100.
Natural gas monopoly Gazprom GAZP.RTS fell to $0.630 after $0.660.
Deputy Prime Minister for privatisation Alfred Kokh said on Thursday Gazprom's control of the government's 35 percent stake in the company should be examined.
But traders said they did not expect a big fall in Gazprom shares today.
"Gazprom shares do what the company's investment consultants want them to do -- I don't think they will fall very heavily," said Andrei Ippolitov, chief trader at Prospekt.
Ippolitov said he expected the market to ease overall -- although not by more than three percent -- today after Wall Street closed slightly down on Thursday.
"It might just be coincidence but the Russian market has been looking very like the Dow Jones over the past few days -- When it's down, it's down, when it's up it's up," he said.
"There's an interdependence between the U.S., European and Russian markets."
